Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 2a) demonstrates marked asymmetry of the pulmonary vasculature with a diminutive right hilum and reduced vascular markings in the right lung, which is characteristic of chronic right pulmonary artery obstruction or hypoplasia seen in Takayasu arteritis. This finding represents longstanding disease rather than an acute embolic event, edema, or left-sided occlusion.
